title: dispatch_signup_meta called with row.id where the test's own comment says event_id must never be the landlord row id
evidence:
+              case
+                dispatch_signup_meta(
+                  meta,
+                  req,
+                  row.id,
+                  string.lowercase(string.trim(row.email)),
+                )
...
+    [meta_client.CompleteRegistration(event_id, _)] -> {
+      // A fresh per-event UUID, never the landlord row id (matches the
+      // password path's `dispatch_signup_meta` contract).
+      let _ = uuid.from_string(event_id) |> should.be_ok
detail: dispatch_signup_meta is not defined in this diff; its return value is the event_id. The code passes row.id as its 3rd argument while the test comment states the contract is a fresh per-event UUID, never the landlord row id. If the 3rd param is the event_id, the OAuth path violates the contract; the test cannot catch it because row.id is itself a valid UUID.
recommended_fix: Verify dispatch_signup_meta's signature against the password path. If its 3rd parameter is the event_id, pass uuid.v4_string() here; if it is the landlord id, reword the test comment.

title: '~4KB header budget' protection claim is false for non-ASCII values — clamp is character-based, not byte-based
evidence:
+/// to `attribution.max_value_len` (the same cap applied at `$set_once`
+/// write time) so an attacker-controlled `utm_campaign` can't bloat the
+/// signed cookie past the browser's ~4KB header budget. Blank values are
...
+pub fn clamp_value(raw: String) -> String {
   raw
   |> string.trim
   |> string.slice(0, max_value_len)
...
+pub fn from_initiate_query_clamps_values_to_max_value_len_test() {
+  let long = string.repeat("a", 300)
+  let result = first_touch_cookie.from_initiate_query([#("utm_campaign", long)])
+  result
+  |> should.equal([#("utm_campaign", string.repeat("a", 200))])
detail: The test pins max_value_len at 200 characters, but string.slice counts characters, not bytes. An attacker-supplied URL with all 8 accepted keys of 200 four-byte UTF-8 chars yields ~6.4KB raw, ~8.5KB once base64url-signed — past the ~4KB cookie cap the comment claims is enforced. Browsers drop oversized Set-Cookie, silently losing attribution.
recommended_fix: Clamp by encoded byte length (truncate the percent-encoded value to a byte budget) before cookie_value(), or document the ASCII-only scope of the cap.

title: find_set_cookie helper copy-pasted into three test files (a fourth copy referenced)
detail: The identical 10-line helper is added to auth_test.gleam and first_touch_cookie_test.gleam, and a third copy in auth_integration_test.gleam admits it mirrors a fourth copy in cookie_attributes_test. Four copies of one matcher invite drift if Set-Cookie formatting changes.
recommended_fix: Extract find_set_cookie into a shared server test helper module and import it from all four files.

title: Initiate test claims the cookie payload is signed base64url but never asserts it — unsigned cookie would pass
evidence:
+  // Signed cookie — the value is base64url payload, not the raw params.
+  string.starts_with(cookie, cookie_names.first_touch() <> "=")
+  |> should.be_true
+  string.contains(cookie, "Max-Age=300")
+  |> should.be_true
detail: The assertions only check the cookie name prefix and Max-Age; they pass identically for a Plain cookie containing the raw query string. If the handler regressed to wisp.Plain, read_cookie (Signed) would silently return empty in production and this test would not flag it.
recommended_fix: Assert the cookie value is not the raw params (e.g. contains no 'utm_' substring, or round-trip decode it) so a Plain regression fails the test.

title: set_once_with_fallback doc claims 'no-op for returning sign-ins' but provider=google is new for every pre-deploy account
evidence:
+/// for returning sign-ins (their original values are already locked).
...
-      set_once_properties |> should.equal([])
+      set_once_properties
+      |> should.equal([#("provider", json.string("google"))])
detail: The modified test proves pre-deploy OAuth signups locked an EMPTY $set_once set, so 'provider' is not 'already locked' for them. Post-deploy, every returning Google sign-in (is_new=False) writes a brand-new $set_once provider=google — the documented no-op only holds for accounts created after this change.
recommended_fix: Reword the doc to state provider is written once to any account lacking it, or gate the fallback on row.is_new if only true signups should carry provider.
